image.subject: a towering American chestnut tree with a massive trunk and spreading crown in a sunlit hardwood forest, golden autumn light, spiked burrs on the ground, early 1900s New England

storyboard.claim: The American chestnut was the foundational tree of the climax forest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a huge chestnut tree dominating the forest
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the chestnut explanation after the blight arrives.
storyboard.addedInformation: Scale and dominance of the tree

image.subject: a pile of glossy brown chestnuts spilling from a woven basket beside split chestnut timber planks and a tanned leather hide on a forest floor, soft daylight

storyboard.claim: The chestnut gave food, shelter timber and tannins to native peoples.
storyboard.concreteVisual: chestnuts in a basket, timber, leather
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concrete uses of the tree named in the narration.

image.subject: a vast stand of grey dead chestnut trunks standing bare across a mountainside, no leaves, overcast sky, early 1900s

storyboard.claim: Within a few decades the blight wiped the chestnuts out almost entirely.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card stating the speed of the loss
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Time compression after the long dependence.

storyboard.claim: The host asks what physically happens inside the trunk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a question card: is it a clogged pipe?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Host interjects with a real question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question that sets up the biology

image.subject: a freshly cut cross-section of a chestnut trunk showing pale wood, dark rings and a thin layer of bark, resting on moss in dim forest light

storyboard.claim: The trunk carries water up through the xylem and sugars down through the phloem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a trunk cross-section with layers visible
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question with the tree anatomy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two transport tissues in the trunk

image.subject: a deep crack in the rough bark of a chestnut trunk with a dusting of orange spores gathered in it, extreme close-up, damp forest light

storyboard.claim: Fungal spores land in a crack in the bark.
storyboard.concreteVisual: close-up of a bark crack with spores
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from anatomy to the entry point.

image.subject: a peeled strip of chestnut bark revealing orange fungal threads creeping into pale inner wood, macro photograph, damp light

storyboard.claim: The spores germinate and grow into the vascular tissue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: fungal threads inside the wood

image.subject: a chestnut trunk with a sunken, rotting orange-brown canker ringing the whole trunk like a belt, bark split and peeling, grey forest light

storyboard.claim: The canker circles the trunk and girdles the tree, cutting off circulation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a canker ringing the trunk
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the result of the invasion.
storyboard.addedInformation: The canker that encircles the trunk

image.subject: a dead grey chestnut crown bare against the sky above a base ringed with thin green shoots sprouting from the roots, dim afternoon light

storyboard.claim: The top starves while the roots send up shoots that are infected in turn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: dead crown above, living shoots below

storyboard.claim: One host blames human arrogance and carelessness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a text card stating the blame claim
storyboard.addedInformation: The first position in the argument

image.subject: a lonely yellow clapboard farmhouse at the edge of a mountain forest in the 1950s, steep roof, uncut lawn, overcast sky

storyboard.claim: The book shows how the beetle reaches the yellow house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the yellow house at the forest edge
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the argument back to the book setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The place the pest is about to reach

image.subject: a young couple in 1950s clothes lifting split logs from a large pile beside a freshly cut gravel road, bulldozed earth and raw cut hillside behind them, summer afternoon

storyboard.claim: A young couple steals firewood from a pile left by turnpike construction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a couple taking logs from a roadside pile
storyboard.addedInformation: Where the infected wood came from

image.subject: a pile of bark-covered logs stacked in the open back of a pale 1950s station wagon, a winding mountain road climbing behind it, hazy evening light

storyboard.claim: They load the infected logs into the Chevy Nomad and drive into the mountains.
storyboard.concreteVisual: infected logs loaded for the drive uphill
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues from taking logs to transporting them.
storyboard.addedInformation: The vehicle that carried the pest

image.subject: a pristine pale 1950s station wagon parked at a mountain overlook with bark-covered logs poking from its open tailgate, soft evening light

storyboard.claim: They act as a luxury taxi service for the apocalypse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card of the taxi line

image.subject: a loaded timber truck and a busy highway cutting through a green mountain valley, aerial view, hazy 1950s afternoon

storyboard.claim: Human narcissism and need for convenience transport the destruction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card on narcissism and convenience
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalizes from the couple to us.

image.subject: a wooden crate of young nursery saplings with roots wrapped in burlap stacked on a harbor dock beside a moored cargo steamer, early morning haze, early 1900s

storyboard.claim: The blight came from Asia on imported nursery stock and spread along highways.
storyboard.concreteVisual: imported nursery stock on a dock
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Source of the blight, global trade.

storyboard.claim: The other host pushes back on blaming the couple or trade.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a text card pushing back on the framing

storyboard.claim: We want to believe we are important enough to be the cause of everything.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card on vanity

storyboard.claim: The other host concedes that humans did move the logs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: punchline card
storyboard.onScreenText: BUT WE DID MOVE THE LOGS

storyboard.claim: Humans moved the log and imported the first infected trees.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card conceding human acts

image.subject: billions of pale spores drifting in a shaft of light over a ridge of the Appalachian mountains with chestnut forest below, wind-bent treetops, hazy morning

storyboard.claim: The spores came on the wind across the whole Appalachian range.
storyboard.concreteVisual: spores drifting over a mountain range

image.subject: a small bark beetle crawling across orange fungal spores on a chestnut bark surface, extreme macro photograph, soft light

storyboard.claim: The wind, beetles and fungus act with indifferent biological machinery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: beetle on fungus spores on bark

image.subject: a swirl of orange fungal spores rising on warm air above a forest canopy at midday, backlit, atmospheric haze

storyboard.claim: The fungus operates on thermals and the imperative to reproduce.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card on biological imperatives

storyboard.claim: The fungus would have reshaped the forest with or without the Chevy Nomad.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card of the inevitability claim

image.subject: a single dead chestnut trunk standing small beneath a vast empty sky over an Appalachian ridge, dusk

storyboard.claim: We merely accelerated an inevitability and are minor temporary variables.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card on minor variables

image.subject: a new turnpike cut through a mountain slope, raw rock face and bulldozed earth, a line of stripped logs stacked beside the road, grey sky, 1950s

storyboard.claim: Human infrastructure acts as a massive accelerant.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a turnpike carved through the mountains

image.subject: a stand of thinned, stump-dotted chestnut forest with felled trunks dragged into a clearing and loaded on a horse-drawn timber wagon, 1900s, misty light

storyboard.claim: Aggressive logging and global trade weaken the remaining stands.
storyboard.concreteVisual: logged forest with stumps and timber wagon

storyboard.claim: We set the table but the crushing power belongs to the pathogen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: punchline card

image.subject: looking straight up at a broken forest canopy where huge dead chestnut crowns have fallen away and harsh sunlight pours down onto the forest floor, bright midday

storyboard.claim: When the giant chestnuts fall, the canopy opens to the sun.
storyboard.concreteVisual: light pouring through a gap in the canopy

image.subject: wilted ferns browning in harsh sun at the foot of a dead tree while thick bright green invasive vines climb over the dry ground, summer

storyboard.claim: Shade plants wither and sun-loving invasive plants take over.
storyboard.concreteVisual: wilted shade plants beside aggressive vines
storyboard.addedInformation: Winners and losers in the understory

image.subject: a lean black bear and wild turkeys searching an empty forest floor strewn with dead leaves and no nuts, flocks of passenger pigeons flying overhead, cold autumn

storyboard.claim: Animals that relied on the nuts face starvation and shift territory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: bear and turkeys foraging in vain
storyboard.addedInformation: Species that relied on the nuts

image.subject: a quiet transformed mountain forest of bare dead chestnut trunks and bright new undergrowth, no people, still morning light

storyboard.claim: The landscape is permanently transformed and no human declared war.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card of the line

image.subject: the yellow house seen from below through towering dead grey trunks and bare crowns of a transformed forest, a lit kitchen window in the house, dusk

storyboard.claim: The forest is overthrown from within while the people worry about mortgages.
storyboard.concreteVisual: the house beneath a dying canopy
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the war language to the forest.

image.subject: a dead chestnut limb lying on the shingled roof of the yellow clapboard house after a storm, pale splintered wood against dark shingles, overcast morning

storyboard.claim: Dead trees start falling on their roof and the dirt always wins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a dead limb fallen on the roof
storyboard.addedInformation: The first sign the people notice

image.subject: a still mountain forest clearing at dawn with fog between old trunks and a faint yellow house far in the distance, no people

storyboard.claim: The place, not the people, is the true protagonist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: text card of the thesis
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the thesis then asks what if someone noticed.

storyboard.claim: What if a human mind could perceive the scale of the trauma?
storyboard.concreteVisual: a question card
storyboard.onScreenText: WHAT IF A MIND PERCEIVED IT?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Poses the question that opens the next scene.

image.subject: a thin, haunted man in a rumpled 1950s work shirt standing alone in a dark pine wood at dusk, head tilted listening, hands hanging at his sides, mist between the trunks

storyboard.claim: Robert hears the woods speaking in a horrific scene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a man listening in a dark wood
